Mission Statement of 
the Montreal YMCA 


“The Montreal YMCA is a partnership 


of volunteers and staff committed to 


the fulfillment of people in spirit, mind 


and body and to the development 
of self-reliance in the individual and 


the community. 


Through its actions, programs and 
services, the Montreal YMCA will reflect 
the needs and aspirations of 

the communities and will work 

with individuals, local communities 

and communities in developing 
countries in achieving social justice 


and control of their environments.” 


©YMCA de Montréal, 1997 


Centraide 


MESSAGE FROM THE CHAIRMAN OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS 


y two-year mandate as the Chairman of the Montreal YMCA Board of Directors has now 
come to an end. These past two years have been extremely rewarding, full of events and 
very promising as you can see from the fiscal year just ended. 


In April 1997, Michael Weil joined the YMCA as our new President and Chief Executive Officer. 

Mr. Weil is back in Montreal after spending several years in Winnipeg where he held the 

position of CEO of the YM-YWCA of Winnipeg. He launched his career at the Montreal 
YMCA in 1979 as director of community justice initiatives, director of the Saint-Laurent YMCA, director of 
special projects and director of the Downtown YMCA. On behalf of all of us, | would like to take this 
opportunity to wish him success in his new position. 


In 1996, we adopted a new multi-faceted strategic plan to consolidate our position and guide our 
Association into the next century. 


As a result, we adopted a new governance structure in December | 996 to increase the efficiency 
and effectiveness of the Board of Directors’ decision-making process. Under this new structure, there are now 
sixteen directors on the Board. 


In addition, the Montreal YMCA began working to overcome its financial challenges. The progress made 
in this area illustrates our accomplishments and bodes well for the future. The revitalization project for the 
Downtown YMCA, which is currently in progress, will further reinforce the Association's financial position. 


In closing, | wish to thank my colleagues on the Board of Directors for their support and encouragement 
throughout my mandate as chairman. | would also like to thank the |,700 volunteers who are involved at every 
level, and who have generously contributed their time to programs, and become members of both working 
committees as well as the Board of Directors. In addition, | would like to highlight the remarkable commitment 
of our dedicated staff toward the Association. Without their efforts, much of what has been accomplished would 
not have been possible. 


! wish the best of luck and every success to the incoming chairperson. 


Cha 


| Michael Novak 


Chairman of the Board of Directors 


MESSAGE FROM THE PRESIDENT AND CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER 


hat a delight to be back in Montreal! After being away for five years, | cannot tell you how 
pleased | was to find an association that is more dynamic than ever. This association 


contributes now more than ever to the growth of spirit, mind and body, while promoting 
social values in the Montreal community. 


| can see that the Montreal YMCA has maintained or implemented effective programs for 

preschoolers, adolescents, troubled youth, seniors and families. | also found that major progress 
has been made in terms of facilities and personnel training. The YMCA has become even more creative in the 
promotion of healthy lifestyles. 


This objective of continuously improving the work we do is embodied in the new slogan of the Montreal 
YMCA: Bringing Quality to Life. 


The recently developed strategic plan is based on the promise that is inherent in our slogan. We plan 
to maintain the high quality of our services and communications. In fact, eight of our centres are currently 
participating in the national YMCA Priority: SAM. (Serving Annual Members) program. The aim of the program 
is to raise our customer service standards, increase membership retention, and enhance the quality of our 
facilities. Furthermore, the strategic plan realistically encompasses the financial obligations of the YMCA. In 
other words, we intend to manage expenses carefully. 


We recently signed a new, four-year contract with Centraide, which will allow the YMCA to support its 
community development initiatives. | wish to extend my warmest thanks to Centraide for its support. We 
intend to demonstrate to Centraide, as well as to the hundreds of volunteers and donors who give us their 
support year after year, that they have every reason to have confidence in us. 


In addition, the federal government announced that it will be launching a national training program for 
youth in the civil service as of January 1998. The objective of the program, involving other cities from across 
Canada, is to provide youth with work experience and employability training. The Montreal YMCA will be 
responsible for placing over 400 youth in traineeships over the next three years. This initiative demonstrates the 
federal government's confidence in the YMCA's experience in dealing with youth facing employment difficulties. 
The Montreal YMCA has a proven track record through its work in employability programs, such as the External 
Manpower Service and Job Generation programs. 


Furthermore, the impressive project to revitalize programming and facilities, which will be launched 
shortly will restore a leadership role to the YMCA. This project will ensure that the YMCA is able to continue 
to fulfill its mission, maintain its drawing power and financial soundness. 


| would like to thank you all for welcoming me so warmly upon my return. The role of the Montreal 
YMCA is as important as ever, and | promise to do everything in my power to ensure that the YMCA fully 


assumes this role. 


Michael Weil 
President & Chief Executive Officer 


Bringing Quality to Life 


The 12 Montreal YMCA centres bring 
quality to life through community action, 
health and physical activities, educational 
services and children’s programs. 


In 1997, the Montreal YMCA was more dynamic than ever. 
lt relentlessly pursued its contribution to the growth of 

the spirit, mind and body, as well as the empowerment 

of thousands of individuals. The YMCA pursues its goals 
through a wide range of educational services, sports and 
recreational programs, youth and child development 
programs, social reintegration programs, training, 
employability and international development. 


A More Stimulating Environment for Children 


A welcoming environment as they take their first steps into society. 
A stimulating environment to arouse their curiosity and desire to learn. 


This year, the YMCA welcomed more than 10,000 children between 6 months 
and 12 years of age. The YMCA provided daycare, drop-in daycare and in-home 
daycare services to respond to the needs of working parents, and to make life 
easier for single-parent families. The Association also provided before and 
after-school programs, summer day camps, and a summer camp in St. Sauveur. 


Accomplishments 


* Anew preschool day camp was started up at the Park Avenue 
YMCA and enrollment was on the rise in the Enfantissimo 
program. 


* Participation increased in the West Island YMCA day camps. 


Children from less privileged families had free access to the West- 
Island and N.D.G.YMCA day camps. 


The Saint-Laurent YMCA distributed hot meals daily to 170 
students at the Enfant-Soleil school. 


The Westmount YMCA launched a new daycare swimming 
program, as well as new after-school and pedagogical day programs. 


The new “Kanawana-be” camp experience was launched. It is 
especially designed for children between the ages of 6 and 8. 


A More Dynamic Life for Youth 


Between home and school, parents and teachers...adolescents need 
to spend time together in a place they can call their own. 


The YMCA created opportunities for some 5,000 youth in 1997. They had a 
chance to become involved in a wide range of projects under the expert 


guidance of people who know how to listen without being judgmental. 
All projects are designed for and by youth so they can learn the values 
and skills needed to live in harmony with society. 


Accomplishments 


The Saint-Laurent YMCA created a student café at the 
Saint-Germain High School where adolescents from some 
sixty different nationalities rub shoulders while becoming 
involved in various activities. 


The Douglas Shand YMCA created a community outreach 
program to better assist troubled youth. The program is a joint 
effort with the CLSC, two youth centres and the West-Island 
Black Community Association. 


The Pointe-Saint-Charles YMCA programs for youth and families 
in the area, such as the Youth Services Coop, continued to foster 
development and exchanges between the French and English- 
speaking communities. 


The Youth at Heart program brought together youth from diverse 
cultural communities with police officers of District 32. 


The Park Avenue YMCA continued its Show Me Your 
Neighbourhood program. 


The Park Avenue, Pointe-Saint-Charles, Downtown, West-Island 
and N.D.G.YMCA youth centres were fully operational. 


A More Harmonious Family Life 


A lot of parents are caught off-guard when it comes to child-rearing. 
They often feel isolated or guilty, and they need help. 


Through its support and training network, the Montreal YMCA was there 
to help 4,500 families take charge of their own lives. 


Accomplishments 


Events organized by the N.D.G.YMCA helped collect 
2,000 pounds of food for the local food bank. 


The support program for Cambodian women of the Saint-Laurent 
YMCA continued, in cooperation with the Place Benoit 
Community Centre. 


Mother and Tot Workout and Support Groups were launched 
at the Westmount YMCA. 


The seniors club at the Pointe-Saint-Charles YMCA organized 
programs, activities, transportation for seniors, and held 
intergenerational days. 


The Keep the Neighbourhood Clean walk had 150 participants 
due to a partnership between the Park Avenue YMCA Family 
Program, Eco-quartier, and Tandem Montréal. 


436 jars of baby food were donated to families in the Centre- 
South sector of the city during the Christmas charity drive at the 
Guy-Favreau YMCA. 


The daycare coop, food aid, Family Film Time and multicultural 
choir were available to the parents and children of the Park 
Avenue YMCA. 


The Park Avenue YMCA created a computer, multimedia and 
Internet lab, which gave 429 people training opportunities. 


The YMCA offered preparation for employment, counselling and 
traineeship programs for youth from cultural communities. 


A More Active Professional Life 


For a lot of people, job security is something of the past. The window of opportunity 
onto the job market has become increasingly narrow. 


The Montreal YMCA provided language and computer training courses, 
as well as employability training for 5,000 people 


Accomplishments 


* The N.D.G. YMCA participated in the creation of a Web site 
for employment and training of the unemployed. 


* The park Avenue YMCA created a computer, multimedia and 
Internet lab, which gave 429 people training opportunities. 


* The YMCA offered preparation for employment, counselling and 
traineeship programs for youth from cultural communities. 


A More Integrated Life for People on the Fringes of Society 


To facilitate their reintegration into society, we need to give the less privileged 
an opportunity by accepting them without being judgmental. 


The Montreal YMCA has launched several projects to help the less privileged so 
they can become self-actualized and self-sufficient, and thereby regain 
their rightful place in society. 


Accomplishments 


* Young offenders were allowed work options at the YMCA 
arena under the supervision of the Hochelaga-Maisonneuve YMCA. 


* The Dialogue project was launched in cooperation with 
Destination Downtown to bring together merchants, 
pedestrians and the homeless. 


¢ Assistance and accommodations were provided for more than 
2,000 refugees. 


* A reintegration program for adult offenders was available, 
including training, professional orientation, 
pre-employability, follow-up and workplace traineeships. 


A More Healthy Life 


“A sound mind in a sound body.” The YMCA seeks to improve the overall sense 
of well-being in people of all ages and help bring them closer together. 


The Montreal YMCA offered a wide range of activities to 19,000 
members and 13,000 other participants who appreciate its unique 
atmosphere. People at the YMCA do not feel they are being judged 
based on their style, shape or performance. People go to the YMCA 
whenever they want, and they come as they are. 


Accomplishments 


* The Guy-Favreau YMCA celebrated its tenth anniversary and took 
advantage of the occasion to launch a membership retention 
campaign, obtain recognition for its instructor training program 
by universities, open its doors to community groups, including the 
Chinese Family Services and Faubourg CLSCs. 


* The Guy-Favreau YMCA was awarded one of the highest 
distinctions for the quality of its membership services from YMCA 
Canada as part of the S.A.M. (Serving Annual Members) program. 


e Several other Montreal YMCA centres received a S.A.M. 
honorary mention for quality and service. 


* The seniors support and development program was launched 
at the West-Island YMCA. 


* The Hochelaga-Maisonneuve YMCA floor hockey team for the 
intellectually handicapped won the Defi Sportif. 


* Preparations were made to launch several YMCA programs in 
the new City of Hudson community centre. 


A More Humane Life on the Planet 


Millions of people around the world suffer from poverty, illiteracy, the violation 
of human rights and environmental degradation. 


Community action by the Montreal YMCA reaches beyond the edge of 

the neighbourhood. In 1997, the Montreal YMCA was active in some of the most 
underprivileged areas in the world. The Association helped local communities in 

El Salvador, Nicaragua, Honduras, Ecuador and Tanzania create their own 

tools and the organizational structures they need to better manage their communities 
on the social and economic levels. In addition, the YMCA organized activities 

in Montreal to increase awareness of the major problems our planet faces. 


Accomplishments 


* The Hands Up! education program on children’s rights developed 
by the Montreal YMCA was launched. 


* The Montreal YMCA contributed to international YMCA 
workshops on sustainable development in 
Honduras, Nicaragua and El Salvador. 


* A-young volunteer from the El Salvador YMCA spent four months 
in training at the West-Island YMCA. 


Bringing Quality to Life

Through its programs and activities, the Montreal YMCA reached thousands of people in 1997.

Commentary to statements 


The audited financial statements for the years ending May 31, 1996 
and 1997 report respective losses of $701,661 and $1,388,005. 
These losses result in great part from the impact of having 

changed our policy of accounting for revenues from a cash 


basis to that of an accrual basis. 


The change in the accounting method has allowed us to 
better manage our operations and has become realizable 
through the implementation of a computerized 


information system. 


The implementation of the information system took 
twelve (12) months spanning over two (2) of our 


financial years. 


Accordingly, the change in accounting method 
created net deferred revenues, and thus, resulted 
in significant accounting losses for the years ending 
May 31, 1996 and 1997.The accounting change has 
no bearing on our cash position and its impact is 


non-recurrent. 


Furthermore, the financial results for the years ending 
May 31, 1996 and 1997 respectively include a charge of 
$489,359 and $606,686 for the net operating costs of 
the Norris building and the Drummond Tower. These 
costs will no longer be incurred in the near future. 


The year ending May 31, 1998 has been budgeted 

to generate a surplus of $452,000, including a last 
time charge of $175,000 for the operating costs of the 
two above-mentioned buildings and we can positively 
ascertain that the Montreal YMCA is financially stable 


and socially relevant.

Montreal YMCA 
Foundation 


MESSAGE FROM THE CHAIRMAN OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS AND 
PRESIDENT OF THE MONTREAL YMCA FOUNDATION 


he role of the Foundation is to ensure long-term funding for the Montreal YMCA. More specifi- 
cally, the Foundation ensures that all individuals (even those who are lacking the financial 
means) have access to YMCA programs. The Foundation also sees to the financial viability of 
YMCA community programs and international development projects. In addition, it ensures that 
centres have the facilities, equipment and programs required to meet local needs. 


During the fiscal year ended May 31, 1997, the Foundation was able to raise $ 258,646 to carry 
out its mandate. 


These funds were derived from four main sources: 


|, Investment income, endowments and bequests 
2. Annual capital campaign 

3. Benefit show by Natalie Choquette 

4 


Golf tournament 


We wish to thank all employees, volunteers and administrators who helped us raise these funds in 
one way or another. We would also like to thank all donors who gave generously once again this year. 


However, the new fiscal year is upon us already with new needs and daunting challenges. 


This year, we will be launching a major revitalization campaign for the Montreal YMCA, which will 
benefit both programs and facilities. The redevelopment of the Downtown YMCA is an indication of the 
importance of the revitalization project. The campaign will require significant funding, of which 58% will 
come from government. We will raise the balance through a major capital and fund-raising campaign 
by approaching foundations, companies and the friends of the Montreal YMCA (members, employees 
and supporters). 


In the medium and long term, we seek to create a more solid and dependable financial base for 
the Montreal YMCA. We can achieve this goal by substantially increasing revenues from our annual capital 
campaign, as well as by expanding endowment funds and bequests to secure the future of the Montreal YMCA. 


14 Pompe 


_ JOHN D. THOMPSON
